verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents Runbooks as its automation engine. Runbooks run workflows of steps and actions according to specified conditions and evaluate those conditions whenever an incident is declared. Documented actions include assigning roles, adding task lists, creating Slack channels, starting Zoom meetings and sending webhooks. missing for 10: documented reminder actions, field-change actions, automated update posting, triggers on incident events beyond declaration (e.g. severity or milestone changes), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, a condition-based workflow engine automates the toil — updates, reminders, field changes — triggered by incident events

citations.quote: Runbooks are FireHydrant's automation engine. They define and automate a workflow of steps and actions according to specified conditions.
Any time an incident is declared, Runbooks evaluate their conditions to decide whether or not they should trigger.
Some examples of actions include creating a Slack channel, starting a Zoom meeting
Automate manual tasks such as creating incident Slack channels, Jira tickets, meeting bridges, and more
